sentences.text: The femoral neck extends dorsomedially at about 90 degrees to the shaft, while the ilium is uniquely shaped and resembles those of Chirostenotes, Rinchenia, Heyuannia, and Shixinggia.
Nankangia possesses a U-shaped mandibular symphysis, which differs from the V-shaped structure found in Luoyanggia.
The holotype specimen was discovered in 2010 by a local farmer in Longling town and donated to the Ganzhou Museum of Natural History.
Its ilium resembles the ilia of Chirostenotes, Rinchenia, Heyuannia, and Shixinggia, a unique trait among known relatives.
Nankangia ate leaves and seeds, as its short lower jaw and non-downturned jaw joint suggest it was likely more herbivorous than carnivorous.
A 2017 analysis recovered Nankangia as an oviraptorid closely related to Yulong and Nomingia.

Fossils of Nankangia are found in the Upper Cretaceous Nanxiong Formation in southeastern China and date to the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, living between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
A 2022 analysis found Nankangia to be the most basal oviraptorid, though this position remains a subject of ongoing scientific discussion.
